endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: However, this modification was not included in the PCCP, and it could significantly affect the safety or effectiveness of the device. Therefore, in this scenario, the manufacturer must submit a new marketing submission for the proposed modified device.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: Please refer to FDA guidances titled, “Deciding When to Submit a 510(k) for a 1370 Change to an Existing Device,” and "Deciding When to Submit a 510(k) for a Software 1371 Change to an Existing Device” to help assess whether a particular change may require a 1372 premarket submission to FDA.

commentary.bottom_line: Two FDA guidance documents direct manufacturers to assess modifications against existing 510(k) change guidance and to file a new marketing submission for significant changes outside an authorized predetermined change control plan, and the final PCCP guidance states this as a requirement. No study supplied here tests whether this practice prevents unreviewed changes from reaching the market or affects patient outcomes.

perspectives.view: No study tests this practice, and no study documents how often significant unreviewed changes reach market. The recommendation rests on regulatory guidance alone. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence, and the size of any benefit remains unknown.

The final PCCP guidance states that a manufacturer must submit a new marketing submission when a modification falls outside the plan and could significantly affect safety or effectiveness. The draft lifecycle guidance points manufacturers to the existing 510(k) change guidances for this assessment. The practice therefore restates an existing legal obligation rather than adding a new one.

commentary.research_gap: Studies could measure how often AI-enabled device modifications are marketed without a required submission, how consistently manufacturers apply the 510(k) change guidances to AI model updates, and whether PCCP boundaries lower the rate of unreviewed significant changes compared with devices that have no plan.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. It remains unknown whether unreviewed changes, such as retraining on new data, affect performance differently in these groups.
